commands.name: random_placement
commands.description: Places player starting positions randomly. Mutually exclusive with grouped_by_team and direct_placement.
commands.notes: Sourced from the Definitive RMS Scripting Guide (Zetnus).

commands.name: grouped_by_team
commands.description: Places player starting positions grouped by team.

commands.name: direct_placement
commands.description: Places players directly, in a fixed arrangement rather than randomized.

commands.name: nomad_resources
commands.description: Adds the cost of a town center to every player's starting resources, so a nomad start can build one without gathering wood first. Grants no units and replaces nothing.
commands.notes: guide:379-383. 275 wood and 100 stone on UP/HD; on DE the amount is the player's own civilization's town centre cost, so Incas get 85 extra stone. The previous description ('a nomad-style starting resource/unit set instead of a fixed base') described the nomad GAME MODE rather than this command, and was the only wrong description in this array not already flagged by verified: false.

commands.name: force_nomad_treaty
commands.description: Forces nomad-treaty rules for this map. DE only.

commands.name: behavior_version
commands.description: Selects generation-behavior version for backward compatibility. DE only.

arguments.name: version
arguments.description: 0 is classic. 1 counts the base_size square inside number_of_tiles and land_percent, and stops land order changing the result. 2 may change object placement.

commands.name: override_map_size
commands.description: Overrides the lobby-selected map size with an explicit tile dimension.

arguments.name: size
arguments.description: Side length in tiles of a square map, replacing the lobby size. Values outside the range are clamped.

commands.name: set_gaia_civilization
commands.description: Sets the civilization used for Gaia (neutral) units/buildings on this map. DE only.

arguments.name: civId
arguments.description: Civilization number for Gaia, which sets building style and unit looks. 0 is the default Gaia. Gaia effects stop working on units players can control.

commands.name: ai_info_map_type
commands.description: Tells the AI what kind of map this is, affecting its strategy choices.

arguments.name: mapType
arguments.description: Ignored on DE, so write CUSTOM.

arguments.name: isNomad
arguments.description: 1 for a nomad start with no town center. Always set it on nomad maps.

arguments.name: isMichi
arguments.description: 1 if forest completely separates the players.

arguments.name: showType
arguments.description: 0 or 1. UP only - not functional on DE. May be omitted: the engine's arity is three.

commands.notes: Exact behavior differs slightly per game version per the source guide. showType is OMISSIBLE and the engine's arity is THREE - measured 2026-08-11 by RMSTEST_54a/54b. 54a put the three-token form immediately before <LAND_GENERATION>, so an engine expecting a fourth argument would have swallowed the section header and left the map blank; 54b is the same file without the line. Both generated fully snow, so the header survived and nothing was eaten. This reaches the same conclusion as a 2026-08-05 attempt that was reverted the same day, by evidence that attempt could not have had: the flag was marked optional on 52 independent three-argument shipped uses, and reverted because guide:475 lists showType Not functional on DE, so writing it and omitting it are indistinguishable in play and no shipped script could ever have revealed which form is correct. A token-consumption test in game is what settles it, not a headcount. The Hard rules that killed the first attempt stand unchanged.

commands.name: effect_amount
commands.description: Applies a flat-amount gameplay effect (resource/attribute/tech modification) at map start.

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: Object, resource, technology or class constant the effect applies to.

arguments.name: attribute
arguments.description: Attribute constant to change.

arguments.name: amount
arguments.description: Value to apply. DE reads it as a float.

commands.notes: Update 185872 (2026-09-22) says GAIA effect_amount changes from a random map generated in the scenario editor no longer carry over into the next game in the same session. Testing on 2026-10-03 found the fix partial. Single player and multiplayer games start clean, but switching maps inside the scenario editor still keeps the previous map's GAIA changes, so a GAIA effect tested in the editor can show an earlier map's changes on top of its own.

commands.name: effect_percent
commands.description: Same shape as effect_amount, but the value is treated as a percentage (divided by 100).

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: Object, resource, technology or class constant the effect applies to.

arguments.name: attribute
arguments.description: Attribute constant to change.

arguments.name: amount
arguments.description: Percent value, divided by 100, so decimals are possible.

commands.notes: Made obsolete by Update 141935 (docs/parser-design.md Sec.8). Still parses and still carries its argument shape — the engine accepts it, so this is a note, not an error.

commands.name: guard_state
commands.description: Sets a guard-resource state; only one guard_state is allowed per script.

arguments.name: objectType
arguments.description: Object or class constant. Use VILLAGER_CLASS for villagers, not VILLAGER.

arguments.name: resourceType
arguments.description: Resource amount constant.

arguments.name: resourceDelta
arguments.description: DE treats this as a float.

arguments.name: flags
arguments.description: Add values together. 1 loses if you do not control the object, 2 trickles the resource while you do, 4 inverts the object requirement for the other flags.

commands.name: terrain_state
commands.description: Sets a UserPatch terrain state. The guide documents it for UP only, so it has no documented effect on DE.
commands.notes: guide:594-612, Game versions: UP only. Arguments and the 0-7 flags range are transcribed from that entry, which is what `verified` records. Whether DE does anything with the command is a SEPARATE and still open question, deliberately kept out of the flag: the guide is silent and nobody has measured it, so the description says only what the guide says. There is no CommandDef field for the guide's per-command `Game versions:` line, which is why this fact has to live in prose.

commands.name: weather_type
commands.description: Sets precipitation and terrain colour tinting on UserPatch. The guide documents it for UP only and points DE authors at color_correction and water_definition instead.

arguments.name: precipitationStyle
arguments.description: 0 none, 2 rain, 3 thunderstorm, 4 snow. Negative values run east to west.

arguments.name: liveColor
arguments.description: Terrain tint in revealed areas. 0 is none and 1 to 255 pick a palette color.

arguments.name: fogColor
arguments.description: Terrain tint in the fog of war. 0 is none and 1 to 255 pick a palette color.

arguments.name: waterDirection
arguments.description: 0 is random, 1 runs west to east and -1 east to west.

commands.notes: guide:613-637, Game versions: UP only. Precipitation 0 none / 2 rain / 3 thunderstorm / 4 snow, negative reversing the west-to-east direction; liveColor and fogColor are palette indices, 0 meaning no tint. Same split as terrain_state: the argument ranges are verified against the guide, DE behaviour is unmeasured and stays out of the flag.

commands.name: water_definition
commands.description: Selects a named water-type definition (must be #const-defined). DE only.

arguments.name: waterType
arguments.description: Water color-correction constant, defined with #const first. Not visible with Render 3D Water off.

commands.name: base_terrain
commands.description: Sets the default terrain the whole map starts as, before any lands/terrains are placed.
commands.notes: The same word "base_terrain" is also a valid attribute inside create_elevation/create_terrain blocks — see the attributes[] entry.

commands.name: base_layer
commands.description: Marks every tile no land paints with a second terrain layer. DE only. This also splits where hills can grow. A create_elevation with the same base_layer grows only on those unpainted tiles, and one without a base_layer grows only on tiles a land painted, even a land of the base terrain itself.

arguments.name: terrain
arguments.description: Visual only terrain layered over base_terrain. Write it after base_terrain.

commands.name: enable_waves
commands.description: Toggles shoreline wave visuals. DE only.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: 0 turns off animated beach waves. They only show with Render Beach Waves on.

commands.name: create_player_lands
commands.description: Creates one land per player, distributing them per the block's attributes. Takes the same attribute set as create_land.

commands.name: create_land
commands.description: Creates one land mass (typically non-player territory — islands, center land, etc). Takes the same attribute set as create_player_lands.
commands.notes: tokenId 32 measured by RMSTEST_62_commandalias_swap (2026-08-12): an arm aliased to 32 made a land, and 24hr_Petra.rms generates lands in the DE editor while containing no create_land and no create_player_lands, so its `#const L 32` is the only thing that can be making them. RMSTEST_61 alone read the other way and could not decide, because its two aliased arms differed in id AND position.

commands.name: create_elevation
commands.description: Raises or lowers terrain elevation in clumps.

arguments.name: maxHeight
arguments.description: Tallest hill height. Small hills cannot reach it. Relative to a land's base_elevation in DE.

commands.notes: maxHeight min corrected 1 -> 0 on 2026-07-31, same cause and same guide phrasing as base_elevation.level: guide:1177 reads "MaxHeight - number (1-16) (default: 0 - not elevated)", so 0 is documented-legal and min 1 contradicted the declared default.

commands.name: cliff_type
commands.description: Sets the visual cliff material for this map. DE only.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: One of CT_GRANITE, CT_DESERT, CT_SNOW, CT_MARBLE, CT_LIMESTONE, CT_TERRACE. Only the look changes. The same seed gives the same cliffs in another style.

commands.name: min_number_of_cliffs
commands.description: Minimum number of cliff formations to generate.

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: Fewest cliffs. The count is drawn from here up to one below max_number_of_cliffs.

commands.name: max_number_of_cliffs
commands.description: Upper bound on the number of cliff formations, not itself included. The game draws a count from min_number_of_cliffs up to one less than this, so the defaults give 3 to 8 cliffs. Setting both to the same value gives exactly that many.

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: Upper bound, not included. The same value as the minimum gives exactly that many.

commands.notes: Default 9, measured 2026-10-17 on five DE maps of a bare <CLIFF_GENERATION> header at three sizes (docs/preview-design.md Sec.6.3 rule 1). The count is min + draw(max - min), so the value is exclusive. The earlier default of 8 was the largest count the guide's wording allows, not the value the game reads.

commands.name: min_length_of_cliff
commands.description: Minimum length of each cliff formation.

arguments.name: length
arguments.description: Fewest cliff segments. 3 is 12 tiles, 4 is 15 and 5 is 18. Below 3 no cliffs appear.

commands.notes: min 3 is DELIBERATE — do not widen it to match corpus usage. guide:1366: "minimum must be at least 3 for cliffs to appear". Six DE-official maps declare 1 or 2 (Fortress.rms:748, Mediterranean.rms:266, Cliffbound.rms:2348, Sandrift.rms:2361, Shrubland.rms:2384, lombardia.rms2:355) and this was briefly read as a false-positive class like circle_radius 0 and base_elevation 0, then reverted 2026-08-05. It is not the same class: those two values are documented as FUNCTIONAL (0 disables circle placement; 0 means not-elevated), so warning on them was wrong. A sub-3 length is documented as NON-functional, so RMS0203 here tells an author their cliff section does nothing — a true positive and one of the more useful warnings we can emit. Corroborating recollection: Fortress declares 5-10 cliffs and is not remembered as having any. Confirm with the three-arm test in preview-design.md Sec.15 item 17b before changing this.

commands.name: max_length_of_cliff
commands.description: Upper bound on each cliff's length, not itself included. Each cliff draws its length from min_length_of_cliff up to one less than this, so the defaults give lengths of 5 to 8. Setting both to the same value gives exactly that length.

arguments.name: length
arguments.description: Longest cliff in segments, not included. Keep the minimum at or below it or the game crashes.

commands.name: cliff_curliness
commands.description: How often a cliff changes direction along its length — low values for straight cliffs, high for winding ones.

arguments.name: percent
arguments.description: Chance a cliff changes direction at each segment. Low is straight, high is winding.

commands.notes: Range/default confirmed; the source guide's fuller description was cut off mid-sentence in the fetch used to populate this file.

commands.name: min_distance_cliffs
commands.description: Minimum distance between separate cliffs, measured in cliff units of 3 tiles. 0 is 0 tiles, 1 is 3 tiles, 2 is 6 tiles.

arguments.name: distance
arguments.description: Cliff units between separate cliffs, 3 tiles each.

commands.notes: guide:1388-1393. The cliff-unit scale and the default of 2 were both already hardcoded in src/preview/generator/cliffs.ts (DEFAULT_MIN_DISTANCE_CLIFFS, and the `* 3` at the spacing check) while this entry carried neither, which is the vocabulary-in-code case CLAUDE.md rules out. No `optional` flag: the guide states a default and never states that the command may be omitted from a script that needs it, and a `default:` notation alone does not license omissibility (BUG-003).

commands.name: min_terrain_distance
commands.description: Minimum distance cliffs keep from water, measured in cliff units of 3 tiles. Only water placed in <LAND_GENERATION> counts, since terrain generation runs after cliffs.

arguments.name: distance
arguments.description: Cliff units kept from water, 3 tiles each. Only water from LAND_GENERATION counts.

commands.notes: guide:1400-1406. The old description said 'certain terrain', which reads as any terrain; the guide says water specifically, and says so twice. The <LAND_GENERATION>-only clause is the guide's own and matters, because a script that paints water in <TERRAIN_GENERATION> gets no cliff avoidance from it at all.

commands.name: color_correction
commands.description: Applies a colour correction preset to the map's lighting. Not visible when the Map Lighting game setting is off, and water is controlled separately by water_definition. DE only.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: Color correction constant. Not visible with Map Lighting off. Water is set by water_definition.

commands.notes: guide:1424-1436, Game versions: DE only. The argument is a colour correction constant from the guide's Season Types list, with no correction applied when the command is absent.

commands.name: create_terrain
commands.description: Paints patches of a terrain type onto the map.
commands.notes: Command itself and the attributes base_terrain/land_percent/number_of_clumps/height_limits are confirmed via a real working example in the source guide: create_terrain DESERT { base_terrain GRASS  land_percent 100  number_of_clumps 9320  height_limits 1 7 }. The rest of this attribute list is name-only (see the attributes[] entries). sectionLocked measured in-game 2026-08-04 by RMSTEST_33a: create_terrain SNOW placed in <OBJECTS_GENERATION>, three runs on a 200 map, produced zero SNOW (40000/40000 base terrain) while the script's own base_terrain GRASS applied normally — so the script ran and this one command was discarded.

commands.name: accumulate_connections
commands.description: Lets later connection commands see and replace terrain that earlier connections created. Without it every connection reads the terrain as it stood before connection generation began. DE only.
commands.notes: guide:1735-1745, Game versions: DE only. It reverts a DE behaviour change rather than adding one, which is why the default is the frozen-snapshot reading. Modelled in src/preview/generator/connections.ts as a stream-state toggle.

commands.name: create_connect_all_players_land
commands.description: Connects the origins of every player land, and of every land assigned to a player. Connections may pass through neutral lands where the terrain cost is favourable.
commands.notes: guide:1757-1770. Spelled with the singular "land", unlike its five siblings. The old note asked for a recheck of src/editor/aoe2RmsLanguage.ts's COMMANDS list; that list now derives from this array (aoe2RmsLanguage.ts:18), so the drift it warned about can no longer happen and the action item is closed.

commands.name: create_connect_teams_lands
commands.description: Connects the origins of player lands belonging to members of the same team, and not across teams. Connections may still pass through neutral or enemy land where the terrain cost is favourable.
commands.notes: guide:1772-1788. Worth knowing when testing: every player is on their own team in the scenario editor by default, so this command looks like it does nothing there unless the diplomacy tab is used to simulate a team setup.

commands.name: create_connect_all_lands
commands.description: Connects the origins of every land on the map to every other, player and neutral alike.

commands.name: create_connect_same_land_zones
commands.description: Groups lands by zone and connects every pair within each zone, leaving zones unconnected to each other. On a script that sets no zones this reaches only the neutral lands, which all share the default zone, and leaves the player lands alone.
commands.notes: guide:1815-1818 says only "Behaves identically to create_connect_all_lands", and this entry DELIBERATELY departs from it. The zone-grouping model above came from two independent community RMS references on 2026-08-06 and is consistent with this project's own measured zone defaults; the guide's reading would make the command a pure synonym, which is not what the name or the community docs describe. `verified` stays false for exactly that reason — it is the one entry in this array whose description is not a transcription of the guide. docs/preview-design.md Sec.15 item 21 holds the RMSTEST that would settle it; implemented as `sameZonePairs` in src/preview/generator/connections.ts.

commands.name: create_connect_land_zones
commands.description: Connects every land belonging to the first zone to every land belonging to the second. DE only.

arguments.name: zoneA
arguments.description: First zone. Every land in it connects to every land in the second.

arguments.name: zoneB
arguments.description: Second zone. Player lands each have their own zone, player number minus 10.

commands.notes: guide:1820-1826, Game versions: DE only. The 245 maximum is the guide's own stated ceiling on a zone ID. The old description said "two specific zones", which understates it: this is every land in one zone against every land in the other, not one connection between them.

commands.name: create_connect_to_nonplayer_land
commands.description: Connects every player land to every neutral land, without connecting players to each other directly. Carries a known engine bug: once used, it blocks all later connection generation. DE only.
commands.notes: guide:1858-1878, Game versions: DE only. The old description said "a specific non-player land", which the command has no argument to express; it is all of them. Two bugs are documented and neither is a transcription of ours: it blocks all future connection generation, and used after create_connect_teams_lands it also blocks team connections except those involving player 1. The first is emulated in src/preview/generator/connections.ts with a SimulationNote per blocked command.

commands.name: create_actor_area
commands.description: Creates an actor area at a fixed map location rather than on an object, with the given identifier and radius, used to constrain later object placement via actor_area_to_place_in/avoid_actor_area.

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: X coordinate in TILES, not a percentage of map width. Must be scaled to map size by hand. May sit outside the map.

arguments.name: y
arguments.description: Y coordinate in TILES, not a percentage of map width. Must be scaled to map size by hand. May sit outside the map.

arguments.name: identifier
arguments.description: Identifier referred to later by actor_area_to_place_in and avoid_actor_area. Multiple actor areas may share one identifier.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: Square radius in tiles.

commands.notes: Full argument semantics from guide:1982-1996, worked example at guide:1999-2011; supersedes the earlier a/b/c/d stub left unresolved when a source fetch was cut off. Three facts the argument list cannot carry. (1) These fixed-position areas are created BEFORE any create_object command, regardless of where the command sits in the script (guide:1990). That is specific to create_actor_area and does NOT generalise to areas defined by the actor_area ATTRIBUTE on create_object, which come into existence as their objects are placed — guide:2782's rule that several objects sharing one actor_area take the radius of 'the first object successfully created' only means anything if those are built progressively. So avoid_actor_area may reference a create_actor_area identifier declared anywhere in the file, but an attribute-defined one only after that object has been placed. (2) Coordinates are in TILES and must be scaled to map size by hand; off-map coordinates are legal and are the documented way to use a large radius to fence off the map edges (guide:1993). (3) The command CRASHES the game if no lands are generated (guide:1996) — unreachable on a finished map, reachable while editing one.

commands.name: create_object_group
commands.description: Defines a named pool of object types. It places nothing itself. A later create_object naming the pool draws one member at random for each object it places, so a group of cow variants gives a mixed herd rather than a themed cluster.
commands.notes: guide:2013-2040, Game versions: DE only. The old description ('places a themed group of objects as a unit') had it backwards in both halves: nothing is placed here, and members are randomised INDIVIDUALLY, so a group must not mix objects with different resource amounts or gameplay effects. Argument retyped objectConstant -> string, matching #const/#define's own name slots: this is a DEFINITION SITE for a name the author invents (the guide calls it text and allows any characters), not a reference to an existing object constant, so RMS0204's 'use a named object constant' and RMS0205's cross-category check were both aimed at the wrong thing. `string` rather than `otherConstant` on purpose - otherConstant is a numeric slot in instantiate.ts, so a group whose name collided with a #const would resolve to a number and silently stop matching the create_object that referenced it.

commands.name: create_object
commands.description: Places objects (resources, units, buildings) on the map, either bare (create_object GOLD) or with a block of placement-constraining attributes.
commands.notes: Command confirmed via two real working examples in the source guide: bare `create_object MONUMENT` and blocked `create_object GOLD { place_on_specific_land_id 13 }`. Most of the attribute list beyond place_on_specific_land_id is name-only — see individual attributes[] entries. sectionLocked measured in-game 2026-08-04 by RMSTEST_33b: create_object GOLD placed in <TERRAIN_GENERATION>, three runs on a 200 map, produced zero GOLD while the script's own base_terrain GRASS applied normally — so the script ran and this one command was discarded.

arguments.name: areaId
arguments.description: ID that avoid_actor_area and actor_area_to_place_in use to refer to this area. 0 means no actor area.

attributes.description: Creates an actor area centered on this object's origin tile. Use actor_area_radius to set its size.
attributes.notes: Description checked against the guide's own entry (guide:2753) on 2026-10-25.

attributes.name: actor_area_radius

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: Radius in tiles, so the default of 1 covers 3x3. Objects sharing an area all use the first one's radius.

attributes.description: Radius in tiles of this object's actor area. Defaults to 1, a 3x3 area. Needs actor_area.
attributes.notes: Description checked against the guide's own entry (guide:2775) on 2026-10-25.

attributes.name: actor_area_to_place_in

arguments.name: areaId
arguments.description: ID of the actor area the object must be placed inside. An object can have only one.

attributes.description: Only places inside the radius of this actor area, made by actor_area or create_actor_area.
attributes.notes: Description checked against the guide's own entry (guide:2818) on 2026-10-25.

attributes.name: add_object

arguments.name: percent
arguments.description: A weight, not a plain percent. The first member also gets whatever the weights leave over.

attributes.description: Adds an object type to the enclosing object group. Since the September 2026 update the weights are lopsided. The largest weight (capped at 99) is the share of draws split among the members by weight, and the first member also gets everything left over, so 50 50 plays as about 75 25. To set a member's chance, give the first member 0 and make the largest weight 100 minus the share you want the first member to keep.
attributes.notes: guide:2013-2040, Game versions: DE only. The 0-99 range is the guide's. The weight is the interesting part and the old description had it as an ordinary percent chance: the guide records the % first not working at all (all members equally likely) and then working as an INVERSE, and flags that it might still be a bug. src/preview/generator/objects.ts reads the weights and deliberately never consults them, which matches. repeatable set from corpus evidence: stacking add_object lines is the entire mechanism of create_object_group (one line per member type), and 43 blocks across the 57-map corpus repeat it. Without the flag validate()'s RMS0306 false-warns on every object group. Update 185872 (2026-09-22) said it stopped the weight being inverted. Community measurement afterwards (Thire7, AoE2 RMS Discord, 2026-10-01, 10,000 units per run) found the rule the description now states, plus two effects it leaves out. The split among weighted members leans toward the largest weight more than a proportional split would, and a member whose share works out near 1% sometimes never spawns. groupMemberProbabilities in src/preview/generator/objects.ts models the stated rule, and the earlier inverse and uniform readings above no longer describe the engine.

attributes.name: base_elevation

arguments.name: level
arguments.description: Height the whole land is raised to, 0 is flat. Above 7 can cause rendering problems. Water lands ignore it.

attributes.description: Height this land is raised to, written on the land and a thin rim of base terrain around it. A water land ignores it. Needs an <ELEVATION_GENERATION> section, which may be empty. Without one the land still rises, but nothing smooths its edge into a slope, so it stands as a sheer step.
attributes.notes: requiresSection established 2026-07-30 during Phase 4.1 engine verification: the section may be completely empty, its mere presence is enough (guide:952, confirmed in-game by RMSTEST_4_negelev.rms). Without it the map generates and looks correct while the slopes silently do nothing, and the guide's author reports in a public Discord message that the map then crashes when played — that second half is second-hand and is attributed, not asserted, in the RMS0311 message. min corrected 1 -> 0 on 2026-07-31: guide:954 reads "Height - number (1-16) (default: 0 - not elevated)", so the same line that supplies the range also documents 0 as the legal value meaning flat. Transcribing only the parenthesised range made min contradict default, and RMS0203 then false-warned on all 461 corpus uses of "base_elevation 0" — the second-largest diagnostic source in the tool. Negative values are also legal (guide:957, maximally elevate; confirmed in-game as 16 by RMSTEST_4) and still draw RMS0203; leave that until a negative shows up in a real script, since the corpus has none.

attributes.notes: Description checked against the guide's own entry (guide:900) on 2026-10-25.

attributes.name: bottom_border

arguments.name: percent
arguments.cautionMessage: Negative border values are valid RMS. The guide's one condition is that the land origin still ends up inside the map, and it names two ways to ensure that: give the land an explicit land_position inside the map, or a base_size large enough. Check one of those is in this block.
arguments.description: Percent of map width to keep land away from the bottom edge (southeast). A negative value needs a land_position inside the map or a large base_size.

attributes.description: Keeps land this percent of the map width away from the bottom border, the southeast edge.
attributes.notes: Guide documents 0-99 as the typical range but explicitly allows negative values, as long as the land origin stays inside the map (e.g. via land_position or a large enough base_size) — so no lower bound is enforced here. Float values accepted since Update 153015.

attributes.name: building_architecture

arguments.name: architectureSet
arguments.description: Architecture set index the building is drawn in.

attributes.description: Selects which civilization architecture set a Gaia building uses. Cosmetic only, it changes the graphic and not placement or behavior.
attributes.notes: Not in the Definitive RMS Scripting Guide. Recovered from the DE install: 72 uses across BR_BattleontheIce.rms and BR_FallofRome.rms, both Forgotten Empires Battle Royale maps, always inside create_object on building-type objects placed with set_gaia_object_only (STABLE, STRANGETRADE, ARCHERY_RANGE, BARRACKS take 2; GUARD_TOWER takes 1) and never on units, trees or resources. The two maps share one template, so that is one authoring decision rather than two - but the value VARIES BY OBJECT within it, which is the evidence avoidance_distance lacked (see parser-design Sec.13 item 5, where every one of its 320 uses passed a constant defined as 0 and could therefore never have been observed to matter). The argument range is unknown: only 1 and 2 are attested, so no min/max is declared. verified: false until an in-game test or a patch note pins the set numbering.

attributes.name: circle_radius

arguments.name: radiusPercent
arguments.description: Percent of map width, not half-width. 0 turns the ring off and uses the default one. Negative values scatter lands instead of ringing them.

arguments.name: variance
arguments.description: Random spread of each land's distance from the center. 0 is a perfect circle, and about 20 matches the default ring.

attributes.description: Places player lands on a circle, with a radius in percent of the map width and an optional variance. 0 turns it off. DE only.
attributes.notes: Range widened from min 1 to min -50 on 2026-08-04. guide:842 documents 1-50 but the engine accepts both 0 and negative values with distinct, measured behaviours, so the old min made RMS0203 fire on correct scripts. 0 = disable, confirmed in-game (RMSTEST_2/RMSTEST_5) to behave exactly as if the attribute were absent. Negative is NOT the same as 0: RMSTEST_27 (circle_radius -20, five runs on Tiny at 8 players, 34 origins) gave mean radius 33.2 tiles = 27.6% of dim with CV 0.44, against the default ring's 50.4 tiles / CV 0.14 and against 24 tiles / CV 0 for an absolute-value reading. Scattered rather than annular, and centre-biased relative to uniform. Not yet modelled precisely.

attributes.name: clumping_factor

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: Higher is rounder and connected, lower is stringier and may fragment. 20 or more keeps a land in one piece. Useful range is about 0 to 40.

attributes.description: How strongly growth clumps around existing tiles. Higher values are rounder, lower values more ragged.
attributes.notes: Documentation widened 2026-08-04. Community sources (AoK Heaven 'The Cartographer: RMS Discoveries') report -100..99 against the conventional 1-15, corroborated by corpus values of -20..100. MEASURED by RMSTEST_38 across five maps at cf -20/0/8/20/40/100: piece count falls monotonically and hits a hard 1 by cf 20; circularity of the largest piece runs 0.133/0.181/0.360/0.409/0.428/0.463; and at cf -20 the land FAILS its declared tile budget by 6.5% while every other setting overshoots by the usual +3-4%. cf 100 is accepted and not clamped, which matters for the 18 corpus uses of it. See preview-design.md Sec.6.1 and Sec.15 item 16.

directives.name: #undefine
directives.notes: ENGINE-VERIFIED 2026-08-01 by RMSTEST_19_undefine.rms, two runs, both agreeing. (1) #undefine does NOTHING: a flag #define'd then #undefine'd still took its branch (7 of 7 objects placed, against a control of 5 that proved the conditional fires at all). The guide's appendix is right, and validate()'s subsumes() may keep skipping the monotonicity check for negated guards, which is sound only while definitions are irreversible. (2) It does NOT consume the following token: `#undefine base_terrain` followed by `SNOW` produced a 98% SNOW map, so base_terrain survived and ran. The `arguments` array below is therefore NOT a claim about the engine, which reads this as two independent statements. It is kept deliberately, and measured: deleting it makes the operand a separate statement to our parser too, which then reports RMS0200 unknown-command on the flag name of every real #undefine line, including test-maps/sample.rms:16. The array groups the line into the unit the author wrote so RMS0310 can cover all of it at once. `verified` stays false because the arity is a tooling convenience rather than a sourced fact.
